skills.name: inventorying-product-capabilities
skills.ownership: Own the exhaustive translation of product requirements into canonical user-visible and system-assisted capabilities before surface design begins.

skills.name: registering-ui-actions
skills.ownership: Own canonical action identity, invocation semantics, consequences, permissions, recoverability and binding requirements across every interface surface.

skills.name: proving-interface-reachability
skills.ownership: Own proof that every required destination and capability is reachable through valid discoverable paths for the intended actor and context.

skills.name: covering-product-scenarios
skills.ownership: Own cross-feature scenario coverage including interruption, recovery, permission, responsive, role and lifecycle paths that individual screens cannot prove.

skills.name: compiling-ui-implementation-specifications
skills.ownership: Own implementation-ready interface specification down to controls, copy, states, actions, focus, responsive transformations and unresolved design decisions.

skills.name: critiquing-functional-completeness
skills.ownership: Own independent falsification of product-wide interface completeness by finding missing capabilities, bindings, routes, states, recovery and cross-feature edges.

skills.name: verifying-runtime-ui-behavior
skills.ownership: Own runtime evidence that required controls, navigation, async flows, permissions, interruption and recovery behave as specified rather than merely existing statically.

skills.name: researching-visual-references
skills.ownership: Own provenance-bound research that decomposes contemporary visual references into transferable mechanisms instead of copying fashionable surface appearance.

skills.name: iterating-rendered-visual-design
skills.ownership: Own evidence-driven visual iteration across rendered candidates, controlled changes and comparative critique until selected aesthetic hypotheses survive inspection.

skills.name: maintaining-project-design-memory
skills.ownership: Own project-scoped memory of accepted and rejected design mechanisms with evidence, confidence, expiry, contradiction and supersession semantics.
